interest: This file provides a concise yet fascinating glimpse into the mechanics of post-World War II accountability and war crimes investigations concerning Southeast Asian collaboration with Imperial Japan. It illustrates the intelligence and diplomatic pipeline linking the U.S. military occupation in Tokyo (SCAP Counter-Intelligence), the State Department in Washington, and the re-established American Legation in Bangkok. Furthermore, it highlights the Siamese Government's domestic War Crimes Commission seeking evidence to prosecute nationals who assisted Japan's wartime propaganda machine.
overview: This file concerns diplomatic communications from early 1946 between the U.S. State Department, U.S. authorities in occupied Tokyo, and the American Legation in Bangkok regarding Yao Suthinun, a Siamese national who resided in Japan during World War II producing Japanese government propaganda targeted at Thailand. Initiated by information uncovered by the Counter-Intelligence Section in Tokyo, the matter was referred to the Government of Siam, leading the Siamese Foreign Office to formally request details on his whereabouts and evidence of his wartime collaboration and propaganda activities on behalf of the Siamese War Crimes Commission.

subfiles.summary: This incoming restricted telegram from Tokyo conveys findings from the Counter-Intelligence Section regarding Yao Suthinun, a Siamese national who travelled to Japan in March (given as 1946 in text, likely a clerical error for 1942) at the Japanese Government's behest. He was employed and compensated by the Japanese Government until the conclusion of the war to prepare propaganda for consumption in Siam. The dispatch suggests that this information be transmitted to the Government of Siam for appropriate legal and administrative action.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 63 from Tokyo regarding Propaganda Activities of Yao Suthinun

subfiles.about: Transmits a request from the Siamese Foreign Office and War Crimes Commission for evidence regarding Yao Suthinun's whereabouts and collaboration with Japan.
subfiles.summary: In response to Department telegram no. 77 of February 1, 1946, the American Legation in Bangkok reports having informed the Siamese Foreign Office regarding the wartime activities of Yao Suthinun in Japan. By a diplomatic note dated March 21, 1946, the Siamese Foreign Office requested, on behalf of the War Crimes Commission, information on Suthinun's present whereabouts and documentary evidence proving his cooperation with Japan and his role in propaganda justifying Japanese aggression. The Legation noted that a copy of the airgram was forwarded to the American Political Adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-5 from Bangkok regarding War Crimes Commission Inquiry on Yao Suthinun
